english.title: Export counterfeit currency with intent to evade prohibition
english.standardoffencewording:

(B)_[shipment as stores]_
(C)_[attempted exportation]_
(D)_[attempted shipment as stores]_

of

(E)_[the counterfeit of a currency note]_
(F)_[a protected coin]_

investigatoraction.description: Criminal lifestyle offence under Schedule 2 to POCA - consider confiscation order

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) For offences committed on or after 22nd February 2024 refer to H102465. Section 68(4AA) provided a specific penalty in respect of counterfeit currency; the penalty in section 68(3) applies from 22nd February 2024.
(ii) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Commissioners for Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs, see section 145 of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
(iii) For forfeiture see section 68(5) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

other.penalty:
Either way:
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a penalty of three times the value of the goods or a fine not exceeding £20,000 whichever is the greater.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex, see section 146A of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
